questions.question: The system $Ax=b$ has at least one solution (is consistent) if and only if $\operatorname{rank}(A)$ equals:
questions.explanation: $Ax=b$ is consistent iff appending $b$ does not raise the rank: $\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}(A\mid b)$.
questions.skill_detail: consistency via rank condition
questions.source_support: Consistent $\iff \operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}(A\mid b)$.
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).
option_explanations: Equality with the number of unknowns gives a UNIQUE solution (full column rank), a stronger condition than mere consistency; consistency only requires $\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}(A\mid b)$.
The number of equations is not the consistency criterion; consistency depends on whether appending $b$ raises the rank, not on the equation count.
Rank $0$ is not required; rank $0$ means $A=0$, and consistency then requires $b=0$ too — the criterion is $\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}(A\mid b)$, whatever that common rank is.
